meta.edit_contract: AI CONTRIBUTORS READ THIS: the shared source of truth is the GitHub repo Torres0990/devildriver-bible (public) — read devildriver.json there, not a cached copy. The unit of change is a NOTE. To ADD knowledge (a new Style, a new mechanic, a new zone): append an object to notes with a unique kebab-case id, a category from the categories list (or add a new category object — build.py generates its page automatically), status locked|decided|open, and an updated date. To EDIT: modify the note in place and bump updated. NEVER change the meaning of a locked note without Sebastian's explicit approval — locked means he confirmed it final. Style kits live in category styles, one note per Style, using the style-kit schema in the style-system note. Bodies use plain text: blank line = new paragraph, lines starting with '- ' = bullets. If you have repo write access, commit directly; otherwise hand the new/edited note JSON to Sebastian and he will route it. After editing: python3 build.py, then python3 deploy.py.
meta.how_to_use: Notes are the unit of knowledge. AI consumers: read the edit_contract above before adding or changing anything; read prompting note for prompt composition. Humans: the HTML pages render the same notes readably.
meta.name: DevilDriver Design Bible (notes)
meta.status_convention: locked = Sebastian confirmed, final. decided = current direction, can revisit. open = undecided, Sebastian decides.

notes.body: Each team owns an enormous demon. The demons duel each other in the central city while the players skirmish around them — fighting enemy players, attacking the enemy demon, and gathering souls to buff their own demon. An unbuffed duel always ends in mutual destruction; souls are the tiebreaker that lets one demon live.
notes.title: Pitch

notes.body:
- Demons are the match clock — everything orbits their duel
- Souls are the only progression inside a match
- No builds, no loadouts — a Style is a complete fixed kit
- Big health pools — nobody gets deleted instantly
- Verticality everywhere — wall-running, climbing, three stacked zones
notes.title: Design pillars

notes.body:
1. Skirmish — teams fight over positioning and the first souls while the demons open their duel.
2. Demon duel — the demons fight in the main city, driven toward mutual kill unless soul buffs tip it.
3. Demon fall — one demon dies. Its team permanently loses respawns.
4. The hunt — the surviving demon hunts the remaining enemy players alongside its team. Match ends on team wipe.

Win condition: wipe the enemy team after their demon falls.
Respawns: while your demon stands, dead teammates respawn after a delay (delay length: open). When your demon falls, no more respawns.

notes.title: Samurai demon

notes.body:
Serious, threatening, unmistakably airborne flying leviathan. Celeste / light-blue body with white-cyan glow accents. Buildings float weightlessly around it so gravity control reads instantly in the silhouette. Not cute, not cartoonish — must read as a rival boss to the samurai.

Kit: manipulates gravity around BUILDINGS only — never directly on players (fairness rule, locked). Makes structures float or ignore gravity temporarily; terrain changes are neutral opportunities for both teams. Asymmetric kit, equal match effectiveness vs the samurai — no soul advantage means the duel still ties. Special abilities, timed ultimate, anti-rider responses, telegraphs and counters.

notes.title: Gravity leviathan

notes.body:
- Boss body: 30K tris (hidden ult arm pair reserved inside)
- Katana: 4K tris each — 2 in base form, 4 in ultimate
- Per demon armed: ~38K tris; both demons: ~76K tris (under 15% of a Quest-class frame budget)
- Weapons are separate assets parented to hand sockets; chest crystal separate for health/ult pulsing
- Draw calls (materials per model) matter more than polygons; transparency overdraw is the silent killer

notes.body: No character selection, no weapon mixing, no skill trees, no builds. A Style is a complete fixed kit: manifested equipment, attacks, defense, movement, abilities. Start with one Style; later additions are complete new Styles.
notes.title: Player model: Style

notes.body:
- Strong parry
- Wall-running and heavy vertical movement
- Demon climbing — players can climb demons and attack body regions
- Structure damage only via specific Style abilities, never basic attacks
- Large health pools — no instant deletions
notes.title: Core mechanics

notes.body:
Tiebreaker for the demon duel. Feeding souls to your demon is the only way it survives the mutual-kill outcome.

Cadence: one soul every 90 seconds. No bank or deposit system.

Open: sequential limited souls vs unlimited recurring spawns vs one rotating active soul; delivery method; whether souls drop on player death; buff magnitude per soul; spawn location rotation.
notes.title: Souls

notes.body:
- One for all (outnumbered): buff activates when one player fights two or more enemies with teammates absent.
- Last person standing: temporary comeback window for the final player — activates only after they have taken enough damage. Not instant, not permanent, not a second life.

Numbers, cooldowns, visuals, and interaction with demon death: open.
notes.title: Comeback systems

notes.body:
A Style is a complete fixed kit — picking it is the entire pre-match decision. Schema for a Style note:

- name: the Style's name
- fantasy: one-line combat fantasy (e.g. 'untouchable duelist who turns defense into offense')
- equipment: manifested gear (weapons are part of the kit, not separate picks)
- attacks: basic attack behavior
- defense: parry/block/dodge identity within the strong-parry system
- movement: how it wall-runs, climbs, repositions — what makes its traversal distinct
- abilities: named abilities, including which one damages structures
- vs-demons: how this Style fights or supports around the demons
- status: open until Sebastian locks it

notes.body:
Target: Meta Horizon Studio. In gradual early access / waitlist as of 2026-10-05; Sebastian joined the creator program. Weekly launch watch runs Mondays.

Confirmed: camera APIs + Monster Hunter-style camera example, custom model import, FBX animation import, AI mesh/texture generation (AssetGen 2.0, animatable characters announced).

Unverified: action-combat netcode reliability, tick rate, melee lag compensation, destruction quality, climbing + animation workflow, physics quality, real-device combat feel, AI character generation output ceiling.

Principal risks: destruction, climbing, animation workflow, physics quality, real-device combat feel. No confirmed standalone export — platform-locked.
notes.title: Horizon Studio status

notes.body:
Compose prompts FROM the structured fields in the notes — never from memory or imagination.

Image prompt recipe: visual_identity + silhouette + palette (as material colors) + distinct features + visual_not (as negative prompt) + 'game character concept art, bold clean shapes, front view, neutral background'.

Design prompt recipe: role + kit attacks/mechanics + match-flow context. Never lock open questions in a prompt — check the open list first.
